basis: Machine-assisted review of catalog titles, summaries and takeaways; official arXiv abstracts or paper text checked for selected edge cases. Labels describe the main contribution of the accepted version, not a claim of priority, validity or completeness.

papers.reason: The source experimental search reports the isolated recoil candidate.
Develops a generic endothermic interpretation; CRESST discussion is a future test rather than a new bound.
Develops the thermal-Higgsino interpretation and its halo-tail dependence.
Develops a predictive off-diagonal-Z Higgsino explanation of the recoil.
Connects a Higgsino explanation to gamma-ray observations and future tests, without evidence here of a new exclusion analysis.
Proposes fermionic absorption and performs a KamLAND neutron-emission recast excluding its benchmark; verified in the accepted v2 abstract.
Constructs a high-scale supersymmetric and Peccei-Quinn realization of the inelastic Higgsino explanation.
Develops an electroweak scalar-doublet explanation with a future annual-modulation test.
Develops pseudo-Dirac and Higgsino benchmarks while assessing existing consistency requirements; the accepted v2 abstract does not establish a distinct new exclusion result.
Derives a solar-capture and IceCube lower bound on the Higgsino splitting that challenges the proposed interpretation.
Constructs a mixed axion and electroweak-doublet explanation with a Peccei-Quinn origin for the splitting.
Develops an inelastic dark-photon explanation linked to a gamma-ray anomaly.

The accepted v2 abstract explicitly develops a singlino with a nearly degenerate Higgsino as an LZ-compatible inelastic candidate, though its main analysis concerns gamma-ray detectability rather than a quantitative recoil fit.
Develops coupled electroweak multiplets as recoil explanations and derives correlated signals.
Provides a gaugino-sector realization of the required Higgsino splitting; discussion of existing solar bounds is not itself a new bound.
Introduces the empty LZ high-energy sideband as a constraint on thermal Higgsinos; identifying a surviving nonthermal mass is secondary to the new constraint.
Fits a generic endothermic explanation and derives a future seasonal discriminator.
Proposes atmospheric-neutrino upscattering as the process generating the recoil.
Constructs a momentum-dependent elastic axion-portal interpretation.
Develops an exothermic fit and derives a sideband restriction against broad recoil spectra; both are explicit in the accepted v1 abstract.
Constructs exothermic dark-photon dark matter and predicts signals in other targets.
Calculates future xenon-excitation discriminants of existing interpretations, without proposing a separate cause or reporting a new bound.
Develops a pseudo-Dirac exothermic explanation and forecasts an argon signature.
Constructs a baryon-flavor inelastic model and checks it against existing collider and indirect limits.
Fits the inert-doublet model to the event and identifies a viable high-mass region.

The accepted v1 develops a leptophobic inelastic explanation; its gamma-ray and IceCube discussion checks consistency and its paleo-detector analysis forecasts a test, rather than establishing a new bound.
The accepted v1 develops a specific SU(6) realization of pseudo-Dirac dark matter and its collider signature; forecast collider reach is not a present bound.
Proposes boosted light dark matter with magnetic dipole scattering as the recoil explanation.
Independently calculates solar-capture exclusions and applies them to three models, deriving the Higgsino restriction and its limited applicability rather than merely quoting an existing bound.
Constructs an inverse-seesaw realization of inelastic self-interacting dark matter.
Proposes a boosted dark-sector flux with sharply delimited recoil endpoints.
Develops a resonant inelastic B-L scalar explanation and a correlated collider target.
Constructs an extra-dimensional origin of the inelastic splitting and predicts target dependence.
Constructs a leptophobic baryon-number model and checks its benchmarks against existing or projected dijet reach.
Fits mixed singlet-doublet scalar dark matter while imposing existing relic and elastic-scattering constraints.
Develops a boosted elastic dark-particle interpretation and target/modulation predictions.
Constructs a singlet-doublet fermion explanation linked to a Type-II seesaw.
Derives independent Super-Kamiokande and IceCube solar-neutrino limits on Higgsino splitting.
Develops GNMSSM Higgsino-singlino mixing benchmarks fitting the recoil with lower gaugino scales.
Studies collider signatures and future tracklet reach of the established Higgsino interpretation; current searches are found insensitive.
Constructs an axionlike-mediator endothermic model and identifies an event-compatible spectrum.
Develops elastic spin-dependent singlet-doublet Majorana dark matter as an explanation.
Fits a light-dark-photon endothermic explanation and discusses existing excited-state consistency requirements.
Proposes bound-neutron disappearance and derives a new LZ lifetime limit explicitly marked as this work in Table 1 of the accepted v1.
Constructs composite dark baryons with a magnetic inelastic transition and a possible accompanying photon signal.
Constructs a warped-extra-dimensional pseudo-Dirac candidate with geometric splitting suppression.
The accepted v2 constructs a mixing-suppressed singlet-doublet model and derives quantitative IceCube limits for thermalized and nonthermal captured populations.
Compares nuclear-response and dark-excitation explanations through target and modulation discriminants; does not establish a new bound.
Develops an ultraheavy nonthermal Higgsino interpretation and independently recomputes solar-capture bounds across its mass range, alongside the high-energy sideband fit (arXiv abstract checked).
Develops a transition-dipole interpretation and delayed-photon test; comparing its fit to existing indirect limits alone is not a new bound.
Develops endothermic and exothermic two-component interpretations rather than an independent exclusion analysis.
Tests and excludes the examined elastic-neutrino interpretations using kinematic and low-recoil requirements with existing external limits (arXiv abstract checked).

Constructs a scalar benchmark explaining the recoil with suppressed solar annihilation. Its detailed revision of capture-to-annihilation assumptions is also a bound reassessment, but no new exclusion is claimed (v3 abstract checked).
Studies the dark-star consequences of event-motivated inelastic benchmarks rather than a new explanation or exclusion of the LZ event.
Constructs a chiral gauge realization of the endothermic scalar explanation; existing relic/collider constraints are consistency checks.
Builds an event-motivated Higgsino spectrum in a supergravity realization while acknowledging the existing solar-capture problem; classification does not imply viability.
Proposes cosmic-ray-boosted momentum-dependent scattering to produce the candidate recoil spectrum.
Extends solar-neutrino exclusion calculations to a broader inelastic parameter space beyond the original Higgsino test (arXiv abstract checked).
Proposes neutron-pair annihilation as the recoil source and predicts companion signals; forecasts are not new bounds.
Develops a radiative-seesaw endothermic interpretation with coannihilation and suppressed solar capture.
Develops a freeze-in/low-reheating endothermic explanation and its viable parameter space.
Compares boosted and inelastic spectra as a discriminator rather than proposing a distinct model or independent exclusion.
Develops an inelastic scalar realization linked to radiative Dirac neutrino masses.
Develops an event interpretation in modified pre-BBN expansion histories; applying existing bounds is not itself a new bound.
Tests whether halo uncertainties can weaken the established Higgsino solar-capture exclusion and finds that they cannot (arXiv abstract checked).
Proposes a speculative spin-2 multi-messenger interpretation linking the LZ and gamma-ray mass scales, despite not providing a quantitative recoil fit.
Constructs a hidden-U(1) scalar explanation and checks existing beam-dump/collider constraints.
Refines nuclear-isotope predictions near the kinematic threshold without directly recalculating an exclusion bound.
Develops exothermic hadrophilic freeze-in dark matter as the explanation and checks its consistency with existing limits.
Constructs supersymmetric sneutrino explanations and checks their consistency with existing searches.
Forecasts an argon discriminator between already-proposed exothermic and Higgsino explanations; a future test is not a new bound.
Proposes DM-induced neutron disappearance and independently recasts Borexino data into bounds on accompanying de-excitation signals (arXiv abstract checked).

Performs cross-model parameter inference and sideband-consistency analysis rather than proposing a specific explanation or a standalone exclusion; boundary with new-bound is interpretive (v2 abstract checked).
Recomputes nuclear responses and critiques rate predictions, but the recorded result is not a direct reassessment of an exclusion bound.
Constructs a complete elastic fermion/pseudoscalar interpretation and imposes existing phenomenological constraints.
Develops cosmologically consistent axion-portal interpretations and predicted scattering directions; no independent bound is explicit in the record.
Proposes a Galactic production mechanism for the excited dark component followed by exothermic detection.
Proposes asymmetric electroweak dark matter that evades the solar-annihilation tension through a depleted antiparticle population.

Computes solar-neutrino exclusions for Higgs-coupled minimal-DM representations with improved capture/evolution and a high-mass response treatment; also refines the solar method (abstract and paper checked).
Builds a Z-prime portal interpretation and combines relic requirements with existing LHC resonance limits; the abstract does not establish a separate new recast (v2 checked).
Studies halo-speed uncertainty and its effect on fits rather than directly deriving or revising an exclusion bound.
Derives solar-neutrino exclusions for event-favored momentum-dependent elastic operators using IceCube and Super-Kamiokande data.
Develops a type-II-seesaw electroweak explanation with heavier relic-compatible masses and weaker solar tension.
Develops an extra-dimensional dark-photon mediator realization of endothermic scattering.
Constructs a scalar-portal inelastic interpretation involving nonstandard quark Yukawa couplings.
Proposes composite-dark-hadron hyperfine excitation as the origin of the recoil.
Constructs a unified supersymmetric realization of the event-motivated pseudo-Dirac Higgsino splitting.
Develops a cosmic-ray-boosted explanation using a finite-mass pseudoscalar mediator and relativistic propagation.
Constructs a composite dark-baryon endothermic explanation and checks existing solar/dijet bounds.
Proposes elastic toroidal vector dark matter and a dark-photon realization; companion predictions are forecasts rather than bounds.
Proposes a screened neutral composite baryon with an elastic band-pass recoil spectrum.
Proposes exothermic pseudo-Dirac dark matter linking the recoil to the Galactic Center excess.
Derives a model-independent sideband-count-ratio constraint and quantified tension across coherent endothermic parameter space; also proposes a future upper-sideband test (arXiv abstract checked).
Forecasts future collider reach for event-motivated electroweak multiplets; future sensitivity is not an existing exclusion bound.
Develops an environment-dependent splitting mechanism to reconcile the terrestrial event with solar capture; applying the existing solar constraint is not itself a new bound.
Compares solar signals of recoil-matched doublets, explicitly leaving detector-level exclusions for later work.
Builds a naturally split scalar dark-photon model and uses its exothermic scattering to explain the recoil.
Develops a mixed-sneutrino explanation with a technically natural splitting and suppressed solar capture.
Embeds a very heavy nonthermal Higgsino explanation in a high-scale supersymmetry construction.
Develops a heavy inert-doublet explanation that satisfies the existing IceCube constraint.
Derives limits on primordial-black-hole abundance from low-energy LZ recoils and rules out the tested evaporation explanation.
Proposes a two-step neutrino conversion and scattering mechanism with a narrow xenon recoil window.
Develops a Majoron-mediated elastic explanation whose momentum dependence suppresses lower-energy recoils and solar capture.
Provides a low-reheating cosmology for the heavy-Higgsino explanation rather than a new observational exclusion.
Predicts a future gamma-ray test of an endothermic interpretation; a projected sensitivity is not a new bound.
Develops an exothermic freeze-in candidate and computes its three-photon decay spectrum to constrain the model using NuSTAR and INTEGRAL/SPI data.
Rebuilds the published LZ inference for a two-state halo and shows that a previously accepted benchmark exceeds the revised upper limit.
Reassesses event-fit parameters under Gaia-informed halo velocities; the abstract centers on interpretation rather than deriving or correcting a specific exclusion bound.
Studies how LMC-induced velocities reshape several interpretations, with no new exclusion identified as the main result in the abstract.
Develops hyperfine excitation of atomic dark matter as an explanation and predicts target and modulation signatures.
Introduces a decaying-parent source of boosted particles that can explain the event through endothermic scattering.
Develops a decay-replenished excited-state explanation; the catalog describes consistency with radiative limits rather than a new bound.
Extends solar capture and annihilation exclusions to scalar and fermionic electroweak multiplets beyond the Higgsino case.
Proposes an ultraheavy fractionally charged gravitino explanation and identifies a correlated multi-recoil signature.
Develops two supersymmetric recoil explanations and their distinguishing spectra while accounting for existing solar constraints.
Embeds the event-compatible Higgsino splitting in GmSUGRA and evaluates it against existing solar-capture reinterpretations.
Builds a dimension-six-operator dark-sector explanation with an associated thermal relic abundance.
Develops a heavy-Higgsino explanation inside supersymmetric SU(5) and predicts future proton-decay tests.
Recalculates Higgsino compatibility under four IceCube cooling assumptions plus alternative halo and LZ-sideband treatments.
Proposes environment-dependent annihilation through an axion-like mediator to reconcile a Higgsino recoil explanation with solar limits.
Recasts ATLAS monojet data into exclusions of elastic operators capable of fitting the LZ recoil.
Develops an endothermic singlet-doublet explanation tied to conversion-driven freeze-out.
Develops a thermal two-component quasi-pNGB explanation with a surviving excited state and exothermic recoils.
Computes solar signals for recoil-compatible singlino-Higgsino compositions and excludes the studied Higgsino-pair fits while identifying surviving alternatives.
Develops an endothermic scalar explanation within a gauged lepton-flavor model and checks existing phenomenological constraints.
Develops an MRSSM pseudo-Dirac explanation and links its splitting to anomaly mediation rather than deriving a new experimental bound.
Identifies a compressed asymmetric inert-doublet candidate and explicitly derives new limits by recasting LHC compressed-Higgsino searches.
Develops a gauged-baryon-number endothermic explanation and its future tests while checking relic and collider constraints.
Develops a modular-flavor construction linked to a pseudo-Dirac dark-sector explanation of the recoil.
Derives current Run-2 exclusions for heavier sparticles in the event-motivated Higgsino scenario as well as future reach projections.
Develops an endothermic pseudo-Dirac explanation whose symmetry-breaking history also predicts a gravitational-wave signal.
Develops an exothermic freeze-in explanation through alternative reheating histories; the existing BBN cutoff is a consistency requirement.
Studies halo-dependent event inference and forecasts complementary heavy-target tests without a new observed exclusion in the catalog evidence.
Critiques a proposed correlated gamma-ray signal through foreground modeling, rather than a previously derived bound.
Develops a dark-Higgs exothermic explanation with two branches and compares them with the existing CMB constraint and gamma-ray signal.
Tests the hadronic mass assumption behind an existing neutron-disappearance explanation using QCD sum rules; it is not a bound calculation.
Examines uncertainty in the LZ electron-recoil background tail, rather than proposing a particle candidate or revising an exclusion bound.
Quantifies how halo-velocity choices shift recoil interpretation while enforcing sideband consistency; its abstract does not identify a new or corrected exclusion as the central result.
Develops a heavy pseudo-Dirac-doublet explanation with a reheating history compatible with nonthermal leptogenesis.
Explicitly identifies new atmospheric-neutrino up-scattering bounds as its main result and judges the attempted recoil explanation unconvincing.
